arxiv-2008-04826.title: Social Distancing Beliefs and Human Mobility: Evidence from Twitter
arxiv-2008-04826.creator: Simon Porcher, Thomas Renault
arxiv-2008-04826.description: Abstract We construct a novel database containing hundreds of thousands geotagged messages related to the COVID-19 pandemic sent on Twitter. We create a daily index of social distancing – at the state level – to capture social distancing beliefs by analyzing the number of tweets containing keywords such as ”stay home”, ”stay safe”, ”wear mask”, ”wash hands” and ”social distancing”.

arxiv-2307-01281.title: Unified treatment of mean-field dynamo and angular-momentum transport in magnetorotational instability-driven turbulence
arxiv-2307-01281.creator: Tushar Mondal, Pallavi Bhat
arxiv-2307-01281.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tushar Mondal, Pallavi Bhat. Magnetorotational instability (MRI)-driven turbulence and dynamo phenomena are analyzed using direct statistical simulations. Our approach begins by developing a unified mean-field model that combines the traditionally decoupled problems of the large-scale dynamo and angular-momentum transport in accretion disks. The model consists of a hierarchical set of equations, capturing up to the second-order cumulants, while a statistical closure approximation is employed to model the three-point correlators.

arxiv-2308-14907.title: Randomized Line-to-Row Mapping for Low-Overhead Rowhammer Mitigations
arxiv-2308-14907.creator: Anish Saxena Saurav Mathur Moinuddin Qureshi Georgia Institute of Technology
arxiv-2308-14907.description: Abstract Modern systems mitigate Rowhammer using victim refresh , which refreshes the two neighbours of an aggressor row when it encounters a specified number of activations. Unfortunately, complex attack patterns like Half-Double break victim-refresh, rendering current systems vulnerable. Instead, recently proposed secure Rowhammer mitigations rely on performing mitigative action on the aggressor rather than the victims.

pmc-10575069.title: Influence of Tilting Angle on Temperature Measurements of Different Object Sizes Using Fiber-Optic Pyrometers
pmc-10575069.creator: Salvador Vargas, Alberto Tapetado, Carmen Vázquez
pmc-10575069.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). This article presents a new model of optical power gathered by a fiber-optic pyrometer when there is a tilting angle between the fiber longitudinal axis and the vector perpendicular to the tangent plane of the emitted surface. This optical power depends on the fiber specifications, such as the diameter and the numerical aperture (NA), as well as the object parameters, including its diameter, emissivity, and tilting angle.

pmc-11403800.title: Spatio-temporal dynamics of malaria in Rwanda between 2012 and 2022: a demography-specific analysis
pmc-11403800.creator: Felix K. Rubuga, Paula Moraga, Ayman Ahmed, Emmanuel Siddig, Eric Remera, Giovenale Moirano, Guéladio Cissé, Jürg Utzinger
pmc-11403800.description: BackgroundDespite global efforts to reduce and eventually interrupt malaria transmission, the disease remains a pressing public health problem, especially in sub-Saharan Africa. This study presents a detailed spatio-temporal analysis of malaria transmission in Rwanda from 2012 to 2022. The main objective was to gain insights into the evolving patterns of malaria and to inform and tailor effective public health strategies.

pmc-11682320.title: Association Between Self-Reported Sitting Time and the Physical Function Domain of the Kihon Checklist Among Community-Dwelling Older Adults
pmc-11682320.creator: Taishiro Kamasaki, Mizuki Hachiya, Hiroyuki Okawa, Kazuhiko Fujiwara, Kodai Hosaka, Takuya Suenaga, Yo Kichize, Yasuhiro Mizokami, Minoru Kamata, Hiroshi Otao
pmc-11682320.description: ObjectiveInterventions that reduce sitting time are easier to implement than those that aim to increase physical activity in compliance with the guidelines. There is no consensus on the association between sitting time as assessed by the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ) and physical function.

pmc-11691315.title: DAILY WORK-TO-FAMILY CONFLICT AND SELF-REPORTED COGNITIVE HEALTH IN MIDLIFE
pmc-11691315.creator: Kelly Chandler, Madeline Nichols, Robert Stawski
pmc-11691315.description: Work-family conflict (WFC) is a potent stressor in midlife linked to numerous detrimental physical and mental health outcomes; however, less is known about its effects on cognitive health. Increasing research demonstrates the utility of intensive repeated measures designs to examine within-person variability in WFC and health.

pmc-12498191.title: Enantiocomplementary Bioreduction of Flexible Ring N‐(3‐Oxobutyl)Heterocycles Providing Enantiopure Chiral Fragments for Drug Discovery
pmc-12498191.creator: Máté Gergő Honvári, Levente András Mócza, Bence Attila Kucsinka, Pál Csuka, Viktória Bódai, Diana Maria Scrob, László Poppe, Gábor Hornyánszky
pmc-12498191.description: In this study, the bioreduction of prochiral N‐(3‐oxobutyl)heterocycles comprising various (partially) saturated, flexible rings is explored using microbial whole‐cell ketoreductases such as wild‐type yeast strains including baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) and Escherichia coli cells expressing two enantiocomplementary recombinant alcohol dehydrogenases.

pmc-12662488.title: Complementary intervention effects of traditional Chinese exercise therapies on T2DM: A scoping review
pmc-12662488.creator: Huixia Ren, Naijin Zhang, Yonghui Li, Yingxiang Li, Mengyang Wang, Huaien Bu, Hongwu Wang
pmc-12662488.description: Background:Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is commonly associated with metabolic and vascular disorders. Traditional Chinese exercise (TCE) shows potential benefits for glycemic control, but evidence is fragmented. This review summarizes current evidence on TCE for T2DM management.Methods:Following the PRISMA-ScR framework, this scoping review was conducted based on the PICOS principle to define the research question.

pmc-13209266.title: Advancements and Challenges in Bioelectrochemical Systems for Sustainable Nitrogen Removal from Wastewater
pmc-13209266.creator: Songkai Qiu, Ruihao Li, Yu Zhang, Hanbing Zheng, Yuqun Zou, Zhuowei Cheng
pmc-13209266.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Bioelectrochemical systems (BESs) for nitrogen removal, which integrate electrochemical processes with biological nitrogen removal technologies, is a sustainable and energy-efficient alternative to conventional biological nitrogen removal methods. However, the practical application of BESs for nitrogen removal remains limited due to technical challenges, and existing reviews have not provided an integrated analysis that systematically links mechanistic understanding, operational optimization, and engineering-scale challenges across multiple BES configurations.

uslaw-usc-t22-s1974.title: 22 U.S.C. § 1974 — Inapplicability of chapter to certain seizures
uslaw-usc-t22-s1974.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t22-s1974.description: United States Code, Title 22 (Foreign Relations And Intercourse); Chapter 25 (Protection Of Vessels On The High Seas And In Territorial Waters Of Foreign Countries). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The provisions of this chapter shall not apply with respect to a seizure made by a country at war with the United States or a seizure made in accordance with the provisions.

uslaw-usc-t42-s5059.title: 42 U.S.C. § 5059 — Legal expenses
uslaw-usc-t42-s5059.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s5059.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 66 (Domestic Volunteer Services); Subchapter IV (Administration And Coordination). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Notwithstanding any other provision of law and pursuant to regulations which the Director shall prescribe, counsel may be employed and counsel fees, court costs, bail, and other expenses incidental to the defense of volunteers may be paid.
